ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Financial Transaction Reports Act, Act No. 18968); Act on the Establishment and Operation of a Beneficial Ownership Information Management System; Enforcement Decree of the Financial Transaction Reports Act; Commercial Act (including UBO disclosure obligations for companies); Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) regulations and FATF Recommendations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the parent entity or Korean Registry Office for the entity itself
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For documents originating in Hague Apostille Convention member states: notarize locally and obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority; do NOT add consular legalization. For non-member states: complete local notarization, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then consular legalization at the Republic of Korea Embassy/Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive paths and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the sponsoring or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Use only the Hague Apostille path if the issuer is in an Apostille member state: notarization plus Apostille. If the issuer is in a non-member state, use the exclusive consular legalization path: local authentication, then consular legalization at the Korean Embassy/Consulate. Never combine both paths sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation and appointment of a resident representative director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign parent company, if any, or the sole incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a foreign board resolution from an Apostille member state: notarize the signatures and attach an Apostille. For non-member states: local notarization and authentication through the relevant government ministry, then consular legalization at the Korean Mission. The Korean incorporator may execute a domestic notarized PoA by the same rules as Korean public instruments.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public (공증인) for the domestic incorporation, or foreign notary for offshore signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Where the articles are notarized in Korea, no foreign authentication is needed. Where any execution occurs abroad in an Apostille state, notarize and Apostille; for non-Apostille states, notarize and consular legalize. The two authentication systems remain mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a regulated financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country bank of the parent entity or the new Korean entity's intended relationship bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For overseas bank letters in Apostille member states: notarize the signatory and Apostille the letter; for non-member states: consular legalization at the Korean Embassy. For a Korean domestic bank, a letter on bank letterhead with notarized signature is sufficient and no apostille or consular legalization applies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copies and proof of residential address of all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority and local government registry or municipal authority of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille member countries: notarize passport copies and proof of address, then apply for an Apostille. For non-member countries: consular legalization via the Korean Embassy following local notarization and foreign ministry authentication. Never chain Apostille and consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every UBO, director, representative director, signatory and intended agent must undergo mandatory screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UK OFSI consolidated list, and the Korean government's own autonomous sanctions list issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. In addition, a positive Politically Exposed Person (PEP) match triggers enhanced due diligence including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, and continuous monitoring for at least six months after onboarding. The Korean KoFIU applies a risk-based approach under the Financial Transaction Reports Act, requiring a written risk assessment and documentation of any asset freeze, designation, or adverse negative news result. All screening must be repeated at pre-incorporation, at bank account opening, and annually for the beneficial ownership register, and adverse media checks must be run in both Korean and English.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (인터넷등기소) at i-erec.go.kr for corporate registration name search, and the Korean named-company registration search provided by the court registry for name reservation status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Hangul (Korean script) under the Commercial Act and the Registration of Names Rules. A foreign-language or romanized name may be used only as a secondary trade name and does not satisfy the registered corporate name requirement. Phonetic transliteration of online foreign brand names is permitted, but the Korean name must include a distinctive element that is not identical to an existing registered name; the local registry applies a four-tier naming convention: (a) Hangul spelling and character set, (b) distinctive word distinguishable from other registrations, (c) business-purpose or industry descriptor, and (d) the mandatory legal-form suffix 주식회사 (Chusik Hoesa). The transliteration doctrine requires a consistent mapping table between the source script and Hangul, and approval officers will reject names that sound identical or confusingly similar notwithstanding different characters.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Securities-type tokens requiring financial supervisory approval under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant or its counsel must first obtain a written rejection reason from the registry official. If rejection is based on an identical or confusingly similar existing registration, the applicant may file a written objection and administrative reconsideration to the Supreme Court Registry Office within 14 days, attaching evidence of a written consent from the preexisting registrant or demonstrating that the existing company operates in a different industry and a materially different graphic or phonetic identity. Where rejection is based on a prohibited token, the applicant must: (1) request an explanatory notice from the registry; (2) apply to the competent supervisory ministry for special permission if the token is conditionally permissible; and (3) resubmit the name application with the permission note, or file an administrative appeal to the Supreme Court Presiding Judge for review of the registry's decision. All appeal submissions must be notarized if filed by an agent, must reference the original task number, and should include three alternative name candidates to accelerate re-filing. If the rejection is sustained, the applicant can seek a judicial review through the administrative court, but due to commercial timelines, counsel should simultaneously reserve a secondary name and proceed on that reservation while pursuing the appeal in parallel.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox address is not permissible for this affiliate media-buying entity because Korean tax law and banking practice require a physical presence at the registered address. The National Tax Service, local tax offices, and financial institutions conducting customer due diligence typically reject a co-working box or virtual mailing address for a Company engaged in performance digital advertising and affiliate lead generation, as this is considered a higher-risk industry requiring more substantive activity. A shared executive office with a physical desk, signage, lease agreement, and staffed access is acceptable only if the office is an actual identifiable suite, the company name appears on a fixed sign, and the company maintains books, records, and at least one part-time employee or appointed compliance officer physically reachable there for tax notices. The Korean court registry requires the registered office to be an actual place where service can be made and not merely a mail-forwarding storefront.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for physical inspection: (1) check that the building directory lists the company name; (2) verify that the front entrance displays a company nameplate; (3) confirm a real employee or a representative works on-site during ordinary business hours; (4) keep original or electronic records of media-buying contracts, invoices, and accounting books at the registered office or at a designated accessible data room; (5) ensure the lease is in the company's Korean legal name and has a duration beyond the tax year; (6) maintain a functioning telephone line or official mobile contact; (7) display the Business Registration Number near the entrance; and (8) keep an office supply inventory and visitor register consistent with active operations. The quantified risk of an unannounced inspection for a digital advertising media-buying company in an active Seoul business district is moderate-low, estimated at 15-25% within the first two years, but it rises to 40-60% where the registered address is a shared co-working mailbox or the company has no visible physical presence at the registry address, as local authorities specifically target such addresses in VAT and UBO compliance campaigns.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Sangbeop), Act No. 1000, as amended; especially Articles 288, 289, 293, 295, 300, 302, 312, 317, 324 and 345; the Local Tax Act provisions on registration tax and education tax; the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 5; and the Supreme Court Commercial Registration Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office of the corporation, operating under the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea, with electronic filing through the Korean Court E-Registration (e-Court / I-RO) system.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Corporation (Beopin Seollip Deunggi Sinhangseo), submitted together with board resolutions, notarized articles of incorporation, Capital Payment Deposit Certificate, director acceptance forms, and corporate seal report.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act of Korea imposes no minimum paid-in capital for a Chusik Hoesa. However, all issued shares must be fully subscribed and the full subscription price must be paid before incorporation registration. Cash contributions are deposited in a capital-subscription bank account that behaves as a blocked escrow until the Capital Payment Deposit Certificate is issued and the registration is completed. In-kind contributions must be appraised and fully delivered or registered in the name of the corporation prior to filing. Withdrawal of the capital before registration is prohibited except where the incorporation is lawfully abandoned.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors of [●] Chusik Hoesa (the Company) hereby records, approves and confirms the lawful incorporation of the Company under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, as evidenced by the corporate registration abstract issued by the Commercial Registration Division of the District Court, and hereby adopts the Articles of Incorporation, the share subscriptions, the share allotments, and all acts of the incorporators performed in connection with the formation of the Company.

RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the registered capital of the Company, as set forth in the Articles of Incorporation and the subscription records, be and hereby is confirmed as fully subscribed and fully paid in accordance with Articles 295 and 302 of the Commercial Act, and the directors are authorized to verify the Capital Payment Deposit Certificate, bank statements, and in-kind contribution conveyance deeds and to take all necessary steps to perfect the issuance of share certificates.

RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company, as specified in the registration application, be and hereby is adopted as the sole official registered office of the Company for the service of legal process, statutory notices, tax registrations, and corporate records, and the Representative Director is authorized to execute the commercial lease agreement, utility agreements, and any landlord consent forms required to maintain such office.

RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the following persons be and hereby are appointed as the first statutory officers of the Company pursuant to Articles 312 and 324 of the Commercial Act, to serve until the first annual general meeting of shareholders and until their successors are duly elected or appointed: [A], Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [B], Director and Chief Financial Officer; [C], Director; and [D], Auditor (where required). Each such officer is vested with the powers and duties set forth by law, the Articles of Incorporation, and the Board.

RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the Representative Director and the Corporate Secretary, acting jointly, be and hereby are authorized to open and maintain bank accounts at [Bank Name] and to execute banking resolutions, signature cards, account mandates, ACH instructions, wire transfer approvals, and electronic payment instructions with any financial institution selected by the Chief Executive Officer, and to designate authorized signers and transaction limits for such accounts.

RESOLVED, FURTHER, that all actions taken by the incorporators, provisional directors, and other agents of the Company prior to the date hereof in order to form the Company, subscribe for its shares, pay in its capital, and register its incorporation be, and the same hereby are, ratified, confirmed and approved in all respects.

RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the Corporate Secretary be and hereby is directed to preserve all statutory records at the registered office, including the shareholder registry, board minutes, accounting books, and tax filings, and to file all required periodic reports and tax registrations with the National Tax Service and other competent authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Korean Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public licensed under the Korean Certified Notary Act, or the e-Notary online platform operated by the Korean Legal Aid Corporation / local notary offices.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators must prepare the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, stating the exact corporate name, business purpose encompassing digital advertising, performance media buying, affiliate lead generation, and related ancillary services, the number and par value of shares, the address of the registered office, the method of public notice, and the names of initial directors. All incorporators or their lawful attorneys must appear physically or via the electronic notary system before the notary to execute the articles; the notary verifies identity, legal capacity, the legality of the business purpose, and the consistency of the articles with the Commercial Act. After execution, the notary issues a certified notarial deed; all excerpts, including notarized minutes of the organization meeting, are made available for registration.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Passport or resident ID of each incorporator
Power of attorney and passport copy for any corporate subscriber
Certified copy of the parent company registration certificate if a corporate incorporator is used
Statement of domestic address and contact details of each incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary rejects the articles because of the breadth of the advertising purpose clause, narrow the purpose to the actual ISIC 7310 activities, resubmit and execute; if identity documents are missing, provide apostilled Korean translations and appear again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription and Capital Payment Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in Korea designated for the capital subscription account; non-cash contributions are verified by a licensed valuer and the bank's AML/KYC office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the notarized articles have been prepared, the Company shall open a temporary capital subscription account with a licensed commercial bank in Korea and cause each subscriber to transfer the full amount of the subscription price for the shares subscribed. The bank will verify the identity of the subscribers, apply anti-money-laundering screenings, and protect the funds until incorporation registration. Upon confirmation of the full subscription amount, the bank issues the Capital Payment Deposit Certificate in the name of the Company and in the amount equal to the total issued share capital. For any non-cash contribution, the appraised asset must be valued by an independent appraiser and legally transferred or delivered to the Company before registration; the latter evidence is attached to the registration application. No portion of the funds may be withdrawn until the company is registered, unless the incorporation is lawfully abandoned.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital subscription statement signed by each subscriber
Subscriber identification and beneficial ownership declarations
Bank account opening forms and corporate KYC package
Independent appraisal report and asset transfer instruments for non-cash contributions, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank returns the certificate with a name mismatch, correct the account title and matching communication with registry, then obtain a fresh certificate. If AML verification is suspended, provide source of funds declarations and beneficial ownership identification for each subscriber; once cleared, the bank will reissue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Incorporation with the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, filing in person or through the Supreme Court e-Court electronic registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two weeks after the completion of subscription and payment and after the meeting of the incorporators has appointed the directors and statutory auditor, the incorporators must file the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Corporation. The application includes the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the Capital Payment Deposit Certificate, written acceptances of the directors and auditor, the report of the corporate seal, identity documents of the representative director, and receipts for registration tax and local education tax. The registry reviews the existence of a lawful business purpose, the proper subscription and payment process, the qualification of officers, and the completeness of the corporate seal report. Upon approval, the corporation acquires juridical personality, and the registry issues the certified corporate registration abstract and the corporate seal certificate, which constitute the company's existence and authority documents.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Corporation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation original and copies
Capital Payment Deposit Certificate
Directors' and auditor's appointment minutes and signed acceptances
Corporate seal registration form and identification of representative director
Receipts of registration tax and local education tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementation order, cure the specified defects within the court's deadline, typically 2 weeks, by submitting replacement attachments, corrected forms, or a supplementary legal opinion. If the filing is rejected, file a new application with fresh payment certificates and pay additional registration tax, or appeal the rejection under the Commercial Registration Rules within 2 weeks.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service for Corporate Tax Status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic portal, or the local district tax office with jurisdiction over the Company's registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days after the court registration of incorporation, the Company must apply for business registration under Article 5 of the Framework Act on National Taxes. The application must be accompanied by the corporate registration abstract, certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation, the office lease contract in the Company's name, and the representative director's identification and seal certificate. The business classification must be declared as advertising and related digital media services, corresponding to ISIC 7310, and the place of business must be identified as the registered office. The NTS will issue a corporate business registration certificate and an auto-generated taxpayer number. The tax office may conduct a brief on-site verification; the Company must keep the real office ready for inspection. After business registration, the Company may open permanent operating bank accounts and receive payments through ACH, wire, and global payment platforms.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration abstract issued by the District Court
Business registration application in NTS standard form
Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Commercial lease agreement for the registered office
Representative director's identification and corporate seal certificate
Bank account details for tax refunds or payment arrangements, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS portal queries the registered office because of a mismatch between the lease and the court registration, correct the registered address in the lease, obtain a landlord consent form, and resubmit. If the business classification is challenged as too broad, amend the purpose and application to ISIC 7310 advertising and media buying before issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Installation, Statutory Books, and Bank Mandate Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's registered office under the Commercial Act, with filings to the District Court registry and National Tax Service; bank mandates executed with the Company's designated financial institutions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation and business registration, the Board must convene to adopt the pro-forma first board resolution on capital confirmation, registered office, officer appointments, banking authorization, and ratification of pre-incorporation acts. The Company must prepare the shareholder registry, board minutes, stock transfer ledger, and accounting books in compliance with Articles 290, 312, 317, 360, and 396 of the Commercial Act. The representative director must report the corporate seal certificate to the chosen bank, execute signature cards, provide a board resolution for banking authorization, and complete beneficial ownership verification. If the Company exceeds the statutory thresholds for external audit, it must appoint an external auditor under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies. All changes to officers, registered office, or capital must be registered with the District Court within 14 days. The banking package should identify ACH and wire payment limits and reconcile with the target payment rails.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution minutes
Shareholder registry and share certificate issuance forms
Corporate seal certificate and specimen seal card
Office lease and management consent forms
Bank mandate forms, signature cards, and beneficial ownership declarations
External auditor appointment form, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank rejects the corporate documents because of missing legalization, obtain notarized English translations and apostilled corporate registration abstracts. If statutory books are incomplete, prepare corrective minutes and records signed by the current directors, and submit any late change filings with the applicable administrative fine and explanation to the registry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - pure digital advertising and affiliate media-buying services under ISIC 7310; no physical manufacturing, assembly, chemical, or warehousing operation is licensed in South Korea.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - ISIC 7310 is an advertising services category that is not subject to a statutory operating permit under Korean law; general corporate and business

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; primary online portal is HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr). Customs export clearance is supervised by Korea Customs Service (KCS) through UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Chusik Hoesa is a Korean domestic corporation, so the statutory TIN/VAT ID procedure is: (i) incorporate under the Commercial Act at the competent district court and obtain a Certificate of Corporate Registration evidencing foreign ownership; (ii) complete the Foreign Investment Promotion Act report through a designated Korean foreign exchange bank when the non-resident shareholder remits capital; (iii) within 20 days of commencing the media-buying business, submit the business registration application to the district tax office with jurisdiction over the head office using HomeTax; (iv) receive the NTS-issued 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which serves as the unified corporate income tax TIN, VAT registration number, and e-tax invoice issuing identifier; (v) register the principal place of business and open a foreign exchange settlement account with a Korean bank for export receipts; (vi) register for electronic tax invoice issuance through HomeTax or an NTS-approved service provider. For an actual foreign non-resident entity with no Korean place of business, the foreign entity must appoint a Korean tax representative and apply to NTS for a non-resident supplier registration number before making taxable supplies to Korean customers; that number is VAT-specific and does not create Korean corporate residence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Chusik Hoesa is a Korean domestic corporation under the Corporate Income Tax Act and is taxed at the entity level on worldwide income. Foreign shareholders may own the entity but the Korean legal entity cannot elect pass-through or consolidated group treatment in the absence of statutory group taxation applicable to the structure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not maintain a check-the-box or LLC pass-through election analogous to the United States. A Chusik Hoesa is taxed automatically as a corporation under the Corporate Income Tax Act, and no elective hybrid mismatch treatment is available to the taxpayer.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea, administered by the National Tax Service.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold. Korean VAT registration is mandatory for every business operator from the date of business commencement, irrespective of revenue; exporters must register even if their only supplies are zero-rated in order to claim input VAT refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-tax invoice: VAT-registered suppliers must issue an electronic tax invoice for B2B supplies and transmit it to NTS through HomeTax or an NTS-approved ASP by the day following the issuance date. The NTS matches e-tax invoice data, cash-receipt data, customs export declarations, and foreign exchange records. There is no real-time fiscal clearing device, fiscal signature, or anti-fraud stamp physically embedded in every Korean VAT invoice; compliance is achieved through electronic transmission and data audit rather than per-invoice real-time authorization.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value-Added Tax Act, zero-rating is allowed for: (a) goods physically exported from Korea when the exporter obtains a KCS export declaration; (b) services performed or provided for use wholly outside Korea, including qualifying offshore digital services, provided the recipient is a non-resident and the Korean supplier has documentary evidence of overseas use; (c) supplies related to international transportation, as applicable. For the performance-media-buying and affiliate lead generation business, the zero-rate is substantiated by proving the foreign client, non-Korean consumption of the campaign services, and foreign-currency settlement; services directly enjoyed in Korea by Korean internet users may be subject to VAT or reverse charge and cannot be zero-rated merely because the contractual counterparty is foreign.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration and export clearance number (equivalent of a customs export Bill of Entry) - required only for physical goods
Commercial invoice and packing list signed by the exporter
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or multimodal transport document evidencing physical removal from Korean customs territory
Bank-issued foreign exchange settlement certificate or inward remittance certificate from a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds

For digital advertising / affiliate media services: signed service agreement, media-buying delivery and performance report, and foreign-currency payment settlement evidence (no customs Bill of Entry is required)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS audit protocol cross-checks UNI-PASS export declarations, HomeTax e-tax invoices, and bank foreign exchange receipts. If zero-rating cannot be substantiated, NTS recasts the supply as domestic taxable, assesses 10% VAT plus additional tax under the VAT Act, disallows or claws back corresponding input VAT, imposes electronic invoice penalties for untransmitted or incorrectly transmitted e-tax invoices, and may prosecute fraud under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. The VAT refund already paid to the exporter is recovered with interest, and export proceeds outstanding after the 180-day settlement deadline without an extension are treated as a Foreign Exchange Transactions Act violation that can also trigger review of the zero-rating claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the foreign exchange administrative authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized but regulated convertibility regime. Current-account transactions, including trade in digital advertising services and administrative charges, are generally freely convertible and may be settled in KRW or foreign currency through a licensed foreign exchange bank. Financial-market (capital-account) transactions, which include inbound direct investment, cross-border loans, issuance of securities, and dividend remittances, are subject to prior reporting or declaration thresholds under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree. In practice, the Ministry of Economy and Finance and Bank of Korea delegate most reporting to domestic commercial banks, which act as foreign exchange banks. Profit remittance is possible without central-bank licensing, but is hindered by documentary requirements: the Korean entity must submit audited financial statements or tax receipts, withholding tax payment certificates, an external audit report if required under the Act on External Audit, and a resolution of the board of directors approving the dividend. A foreign exchange bank will then endorse the dividend remittance declaration. No separate central bank approval is generally required for ordinary dividends, but funds derived from capital transactions must be supported by underlying documentation to avoid disguised outward remittance. Accordingly, the won is effectively convertible for trading and profit repatriation, with procedural friction centered on KYC and FX reporting rather than absolute convertibility denial.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory conversion ratio is imposed; 0% of export proceeds must be surrendered in KRW. All export-related foreign currency receipts must be collected within six months from the date of export declaration and must be either sold to a domestic foreign exchange bank or credited to a foreign currency account established with such a bank; extension and rollover are permitted upon bank certification and regulatory reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW corporate checking plus USD foreign currency account)
Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW corporate checking plus USD foreign currency account)
Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW corporate checking plus USD foreign currency account)
Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW corporate checking plus USD foreign currency account)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as a primary banking relationship. Offshore digital EMIs such as Mercury, Wise, and Airwallex are not chartered as commercial banks in South Korea and are not licensed to execute corporate foreign exchange transactions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Korean regulations require cross-border remittance and FX settlement to be routed through a licensed foreign exchange bank; unauthorized cross-border payment services can expose the delivering institution to criminal and administrative sanctions. EMIs may only serve as complementary rails for low-value operational payments to overseas ad networks, and cannot receive foreign direct investment, satisfy statutory capital verification, or replace the Korean domestic bank account required for tax and regulatory filings. Therefore the legal onboarding blueprint must rely on domestic Tier-1 banks for the core treasury, with EMIs confined to non-qualifying overflow channels strictly as a supplementary option.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed Chusik Hoesa, the statutory representative director or an authorized signatory with a notarized power of attorney must physically appear at the Korean bank branch for verification. Remote video verification is acceptable for Korean nationals or residents with recognized certified public certificates, but foreign non-resident directors are generally not eligible. Consular proxy account opening is not recognized under the Real Name Financial Transaction Act and the corporate account opening policy of Korean commercial banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore nominee shareholder or undisclosed economic interest in the Chusik Hoesa
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Corporate Registry Extract from the competent Korean court; shareholder register ledger showing natural persons' names, masked resident numbers, and exact shareholding percentages; signed Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) declaration; source-of-wealth letters from every direct and indirect beneficial owner above 25%; notarized passport copies; no-nominee undertaking; and an organisational chart evidencing the full control chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Affiliate media buying and performance marketing flagged as high-risk digital payment intermediation with third-party funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master services agreements with advertisers and publishers; official partner or agency certificates from major platforms such as Google Ads and Meta Business Partners; monthly media-spend reports; itemized invoices from supply-side platforms and ad networks; a documented sub-affiliate treatment policy; a whitelist of sanctioned-counterparty screening results; and a written compliance policy prohibiting fraudulent traffic, click farms, and digital asset settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inadequate physical substance and business continuity for a newly incorporated Korean entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office lease agreement with rent payment receipts; proof of payment for telecommunication and utility bills; employment contracts and payroll records of at least one resident director or locally engaged employee holding a valid Korean work visa; Korean Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance and National Health Insurance filings; and a business continuity plan describing continued trading arrangements and liquidated-traffic escrow procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent FX purpose and irregular cash flows to overseas payees in high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letters from current or previous counterparty banks; Know-Your-Business dossiers on overseas publishers and media vendors; service agreements and statement-of-work documents; evidence of active digital ad platform accounts through Google Ads Manager (MCC) or Meta Business Manager; the initial six-month treasury ledger with projected transaction volumes; and approved Foreign Exchange Transactions Act purpose codes assigned by the responsible foreign exchange bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders must structure the capital contribution as a foreign direct investment (FDI) report filed with a delegated domestic foreign exchange bank before or at the time of receipt. The funds are transmitted via SWIFT MT103 wire with the beneficiary and reference details clearly indicating 'FDI under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Article 15 of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act'. The Korean corporation opens a temporary foreign investment capital account with a Tier-1 bank, receives the incoming KRW or USD, and then files the Foreign Investment Enterprise Registration after the new shares are issued. The bank marks the purpose code in accordance with the Bank of Korea Foreign Exchange Transaction Classification, and a Korean certified public accountant may issue a capital verification report if requested by the bank or the foreign exchange authorities. This routing ensures statutory approval, correct FX designation, and clean capital verification for subsequent dividend remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For digital advertising media buying and affiliate services, the standard clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 with the underlying service agreement, invoices, and tax certificates attached for the foreign exchange bank's documentary review. For physical-goods trade or media procurement requiring transactional evidence, commercial letters of credit and documentary collections may be used through the same Tier-1 bank. Payments for services above USD 50,000 require submission of the contract, invoice, and perhaps a certified copy of the Korean trade report to the bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Settlement is normally executed in USD or KRW through the bank's correspondent network; crypto-asset settlement or routing through unauthorised electronic money institutions is prohibited. The account bank must file the outbound payment declaration before returning the MT103 confirmation to the remitter.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/KRW forward contracts (covered forwards up to 12 months) permissible only when there is a genuine underlying current-account or capital-account exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted for non-resident counterparties hedging KRW-denominated exposures or for resident exporters with a documented USD receivable

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) and USD/KRW cross-currency swaps with licensed foreign exchange banks for long-term balance-sheet hedging of foreign capital injections; speculative use is expressly prohibited

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) convening, presentation of statutory financial statements, business report, and approval of profit appropriation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the Chusik Hoesa; internal statutory governance requirement under the Korean Commercial Act, Article 365
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the AGM must be held no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to convene the AGM may be subject to an administrative fine of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,700); failure to prepare or preserve statutory minutes may attract summary fines; repeated failure may expose directors to civil and criminal liability and a court-ordered AGM upon shareholder petition.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return, including statutory financial statements, tax reconciliation schedules, and depreciation/attenuating schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the third month after the fiscal year-end; for December 31 fiscal year-end, due by March 31; one-month extension is available upon application and security approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under-reporting penalty of 20% of the understated tax, fraudulent or failure-to-file penalty of 40% of the unpaid tax, plus late-payment interest of 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum); unpaid tax over six months triggers NTS asset seizure, business registration downgrade, and possible compulsory closure of the business as an administrative forfeiture trigger.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax (surtax) return matching the national corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government of the head office jurisdiction (Si/Gun/Gu) through the Local Tax Information System (We Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the national corporate income tax return; for December 31 fiscal year-end, due by March 31, or by the extended national filing date if such extension is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional local tax of 20% for under-reporting, 40% for failure to file, plus 0.022% daily late-payment interest; continued delinquency can lead to local tax compulsory collection, seizure, and closure of the local business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual value-added tax (VAT) returns and payments for VAT-registered advertising and media-buying operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half-year (January 1-June 30) return due by July 25; second half-year (July 1-December 31) return due by January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omitted or under-declared VAT attracts an additional 10% penalty, with a 20% penalty for fraudulent omission and 0.022% daily late-payment interest; persistent non-filing can result in NTS estimation, asset seizure, and administrative cancellation of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer withholding tax finalization (year-end payroll settlement) and withholding payment summaries for employees, including cross-border affiliate payments if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual employer withholding summary and employee income tax reconciliation due by March 10 after the income year; monthly withholding remittances are due by the 10th of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid withheld taxes attract the standard non-declaration penalty and daily 0.022% late-payment interest; continued failure to remit employee withholding taxes can lead to criminal penalties for the representative director, NTS seizure, and administrative revocation of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent statutory external audit report and audited financial statements required for companies subject to the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting; for externally audited companies, the audit opinion and financial statements are filed with and disclosed through the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) DART system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Auditor's report must be submitted to the board before the AGM and delivered to shareholders no later than one week before the AGM; audited financial statements must be filed with the AGM package by the AGM date, which must occur within three months of fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A company that fails to obtain a mandatory external audit will be designated as an audit-omission company; the Financial Services Commission may impose administrative fines and issue corrective orders; the company may lose tax incentives, be subject to additional inspection, and its directors may face fines under the external audit law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment shareholding change report and beneficial-owner refresh filing for any non-resident shareholder, share transfer, capital increase, or change in direct/indirect foreign ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA or the Foreign Investment Information System under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days from the date of the relevant share acquisition, transfer, or foreign-investment change; no separate annual UBO return is required for ordinary unlisted Chusik Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the post-change foreign investment report may result in administrative fines, suspension or revocation of foreign investment benefits, and adverse tax-treaty or foreign-exchange sanction consequences.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent certified public accountant audit applies under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies if, as of the preceding fiscal year-end, the Chusik Hoesa meets any of the following: (i) total assets equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9.1 million); (ii) the company is listed or is a public-interest corporation; (iii) total assets equal or exceed KRW 7,000,000,000 and the company does not qualify as a small corporation under the statutory 'small company' exemption, including headcount/employee scale criteria under the Presidential Decree; or (iv) the Financial Services Commission or Financial Supervisory Service specifically designates the company for external audit. There is no general turnover-only trigger, but revenue and headcount scale are used to determine the small-company exemption and applicability of the delegated thresholds. All externally audited companies must use a licensed CPA audit firm registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for public-interest companies and companies required under the external audit framework to apply K-IFRS; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP / SME Accounting Standards) for non-listed small and medium Chusik Hoesa; financial statements attached to the corporate tax return must be prepared in accordance with the Corporate Tax Act requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not currently impose a separate annual universal beneficial-owner return for ordinary unlisted Chusik Hoesa. Legal compliance operates through the following annual and event-driven protocol: (i) the shareholder register must be updated immediately upon any share transfer and presented for inspection at the AGM; (ii) any transfer of shares or change in direct or indirect foreign ownership must be reported to MOTIE/KOTRA within 30 days under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; (iii) the annual corporate income tax return must disclose the shareholder list, controlling shareholders, and related-party arrangements; (iv) financial institutions engaging with the entity will refresh customer due diligence and beneficial-owner information on a periodic basis under the Financial Transactions Reports Act; and (v) the AGM approval of the share register and financial statements constitutes the annual confirmation of ownership records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Statutory Auditors
Register of Charges, Mortgages, and Pledges on Shares
Minute Book of Shareholders Meetings and Board of Directors Meetings
Business Registration Certificate displayed at the head office

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 800 to 2,000 typical annual fee for a Korean registered office, local correspondence address, and secretarial maintenance for an unlisted Chusik Hoesa
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 6,000 to 25,000 for a small or medium advertising and media-buying Chusik Hoesa; 25,000 to 75,000 if consolidated K-IFRS group reporting or a larger audit scope is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% (national corporate income tax rate on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korean local income tax surtax of 10% on national corporate tax, yielding an effective headline rate of 26.4%. Statutory incentives include tax holidays under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, i.e., Regional Tax Credit for job creation and facility investment, Six Sigma or R&D tax credit, foreign investment tax credit, and compatibility with foreign-investor incentives for high-tech businesses. No patent box regime exists, but intangible expenses may benefit from R&D tax credits if used for Korean-source business.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Tax Return (Form 1) filed electronically via the National Tax Service HomeTax system. The filing package includes the main return, financial statements, statement of taxable income computation, and tax adjustment schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end. Upon application for extension, the deadline may be extended by up to three months for qualifying corporations, provided the tax liability is prepaid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total sales revenue from business operations including affiliate media buying commissions, lead generation proceeds, and digital advertising arbitrage revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owned Korean entities must include all worldwide revenue attributable to the domestic business. For affiliate media buying, gross revenue must not be reduced by phantom rebates or unrealized affiliate clawbacks; timing of revenue recognition follows Korean GAAP. The IP holder and the Korean sales entity must be distinct; transfer pricing adjustments arising from sales commissions to foreign parent companies must be declared as separate adjustment entries in the tax reconciliation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends received from Korean subsidiaries, certain government subsidies, and other statutory non-taxable income items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders receiving dividends from a Korean Chusik Hoesa must track dividends at the shareholder level; Box 2 accepts only income that qualifies as non-taxable for the Korean entity under the Corporate Tax Act, not income exempted for the foreign shareholder. Intercompany dividends from foreign CFCs must be reviewed against CFC rules and must not be used to avoid Korean corporate tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Cost of Sales and Ordinary Business Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Media buying costs, ad network fees, performance-based affiliate payouts, SaaS subscription costs, personnel expenses, and office overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean media-buying affiliate, expense deductions must be supported by third-party invoices, media panel reports, and bank remittance records. Payments for intangible ad technology royalties or foreign consultancy fees require an international tax reporting form attached to the return. Failure to file Form 10-2 (international transactions) invalidates the deduction and triggers a 20% underreporting penalty. Expense allocations must be made on an arm's length basis, especially when a foreign parent provides ad inventory or algorithmic bidding services.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation on fixed assets and amortization of intangible assets such as software licenses, patents, trademarks, and purchased client lists.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korean GAAP rates and useful lives must be used. For media buying platforms, software development costs capitalized in Korea or paid to a foreign group company require economic ownership analysis; the foreign entity cannot amortize Korean-sourced digital assets unless it has Korean tax nexus. Amortization on goodwill is not deductible in Korea; instead, impairment losses may be recognized under strictly audited conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Taxable Income before Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit per Korean GAAP adjusted by tax-specific add-backs and deductions without loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for entertainment expenses in excess of statutory limit, political contributions, and non-deductible membership fees. For non-resident controlled entities, excessive management fees, sharing of group overhead, and transfer pricing corrections must be added back unless an Advance Pricing Agreement has been executed with the NTS. The adjusted income must equal the ordinary income per the Korean statutory income reconciliation format.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of prior-year net operating losses within the 5-year carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent acquiring a Korean loss company cannot freely use pre-acquisition losses if the business control changed with the intention of acquiring tax benefits; the anti-trafficking rule under Article 55 of the Corporate Tax Act disallows such deductions. Losses from foreign permanent establishments cannot offset domestic Korean source income except under the foreign tax credit method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Special Tax Credits (Foreign Tax Credit and R&D Credit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits for foreign taxes paid on Korean-source income and for qualified R&D expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign investors may claim foreign tax credits for withholding taxes on inbound dividends, interest, and royalties, but the credit must be calculated on a per-country basis. The Korean entity must prove that taxes paid abroad correspond to income already included in the Korean tax base. Non-documentation of the residency certificate invalidates credit claims.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under Article 75 of the Framework Act on Public International Tax: 20% of the unpaid tax plus 40% additional penalty for unfaithful filing or 10-20% for unlawful foreign tax refunds. Daily late payment surcharge of 0.03% of unpaid tax accrues until payment. Criminal liability applies under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: imprisonment up to 3 years and fines up to 3 times the evaded tax. Habitual or aggravated evasion can raise imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national corporate income tax withholding on dividends to non-residents plus 2% local income tax surtax, equal to 10% of the national tax)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate, the Korean withholding agent or the foreign beneficial owner must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority and include a certified Korean translation; (2) submit the DTA Relief Application Form (Form 18-) to the local branch tax office through HomeTax before or concurrently with the withholding return; (3) evidence beneficial ownership through board resolutions, ownership structure charts, underlying business substance, and financing documents; (4) identify the foreign entity as the true recipient, not a conduit, under the limitation-on-benefits clause; (5) maintain all records for at least five years. If the full 22% withholding is levied, reclaim the excess through the NTS refund procedure within the statutory statute of limitations (generally five years).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding is 22% each for royalties and intercompany interest paid to non-residents (20% national plus 2% local). Treaty rates vary by DTA: typically 10-15% for interest and 5-10% for royalties subject to beneficial ownership and anti-treaty-shopping rules. Royalties for use or transfer of industrial/commercial know-how may carry a 22% statutory tax and need a Form 13- attached to the payment. Interest on convertible bonds or profit participating loans is treated as dividend if the payment is dependent on earnings.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is required if foreign-related party transactions in any category exceed KRW 5 billion in a fiscal year. Master File is required if total revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and foreign-related party transactions exceed KRW 50 billion. Simplified documentation applies for transactions below KRW 5 billion, but the taxpayer must still prepare contemporaneous evidence upon NTS audit.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime analogous to UAE, but the Corporate Tax Act and the Framework Act on International Tax incorporate a substantive economic-substance requirement and General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR). The NTS will pierce transactions lacking commercial rationale, with Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) defined by: the location of board meetings, where ad-buying employees perform their duties, where the algorithmic bidding servers are legally owned, where media contracts are signed, and where treasury/finance staff exercise cash management. Shell media-buying structures where a Korean Chusik Hoesa merely invoices foreign affiliate networks, while employees and technology remain outside Korea, will be recharacterized or assessed under CFC rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording fabricated digital advertising invoices from a related shell company or issuing fraudulent purchase confirmations for media inventory that never existed, thereby reducing taxable income to near zero.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: imprisonment for up to 3 years or a fine not exceeding 3 times the evaded tax. Under the Corporate Tax Act, a 20% misstatement penalty and daily late-payment surcharge of 0.03% apply. Intentional fabrication also triggers Article 178 of the Criminal Act for false tax document creation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts shall pierce the corporate veil under Korean Commercial Act Article 401 to hold directors personally liable for gross negligence or malicious behavior. The NTS may collect unpaid corporate tax directly from the director's personal assets and may impose a travel ban (blacklisting) for tax delinquency above KRW 500 million. Convicted directors face imprisonment up to 3 years, disqualification from serving as directors, and disgorgement of personal wealth traceable to the offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Abuse / Artificial Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manipulating affiliate commission ratios, algorithmic-bidding profit splits, or ad-network cost pass-throughs to shift Korean operating profit to a low-tax foreign parent or a Hong Kong/SG related party without functional or risk allocation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 4 and 5 of the Act on Coordination of International Tax Affairs (ACITA): the NTS imposes upward arm's length income adjustment with 10-year limitations. Penalties include 20% of the unreported adjustment plus 0.03% daily surcharge. ACITA also authorizes secondary adjustment re-characterizing unrepatriated profits as deemed dividends or loans, triggering further withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed fabricated intercompany agreements are individually liable under Commercial Act Article 401 for damage caused to the Korean entity and creditors. The court can order restoration of foreign assets and personal seizure of the director's bank accounts. Criminal antitrust/intentional tax evasion may result in imprisonment up to 3 years and a travel ban; the NTS can also block dispatch to overseas business due to delinquent status.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Misuse of DTA / Shell Company Beneficial Ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Chusik Hoesa routes royalty, dividend, or media-arbitrage payments through a paper holding company in a treaty jurisdiction solely to obtain a reduced 5% DTA withholding rate while the holding company has no personnel, no assets, and no decision-making power.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: NTS denies treaty benefits under the beneficial ownership requirement and the GAAR in Article 10-2 ACITA. The taxpayer must pay the full 22% withholding plus 20% deficiency penalty and daily late surcharge. The foreign recipient is treated as having a Korean permanent establishment, and 100% of the income becomes subject to Korean corporate tax through branch filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Third-party creditor claims and the Korean entity's claims can be levied directly against directors who authorized the sham transaction. Under the Commercial Act and tax crime law, directors face joint and several liability for the hidden tax liability, criminal imprisonment up to 3 years, and restriction of departure. The court may pierce the foreign holding entity's corporate veil and seize the personal bank accounts of Korean-resident directors and all title over Korean assets.
